papers.title: Nonvolatile single-ion memory with picosecond switching
authors: Chengjie Zuo School of Integrated Circuits
Cas Center for Excellence in Quantum Information
Materials ScienceKey Laboratory of Magnetic Molecules
Magnetic Materials of the Ministry of Education
papers.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), and edge computing applications has posed severe challenges to conventional memory technologies in terms of density, speed, and energy consumption. Herein, a single-ion transport mechanism is proposed to achieve picosecond (ps) switching capability. For monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) with single-atom vacancy defects, first-principles calculations reveal that single-ion penetration across the BN plane dominates the resistive switching. The trapping and release of a single ion correspond to different states of the memory device for one bit of information. Experimentally fabricated single-ion memory exhibits nonvolatile resistive switching with ultra-fast switching speed of 20 ps and ultra-low energy consumption of 310 aJ/bit. This high performance is attributed to the extremely short distance for the single ion to travel through. Such devices pave the way for the realization of high-performance nonvolatile memory with ultra-fast speed, ultra-low energy consumption, and high storage density, that is called the"Unified Memory"long desired by the whole industry.

papers.title: Euclid. I. Overview of the Euclid mission
papers.abstract: The current standard model of cosmology successfully describes a variety of measurements, but the nature of its main ingredients, dark matter and dark energy, remains unknown. is a medium-class mission in the Cosmic Vision 2015--2025 programme of the European Space Agency (ESA) that will provide high-resolution optical imaging, as well as near-infrared imaging and spectroscopy, over about 14\,000\,deg$^2$ of extragalactic sky. In addition to accurate weak lensing and clustering measurements that probe structure formation over half of the age of the Universe, its primary probes for cosmology, these exquisite data will enable a wide range of science. This paper provides a high-level overview of the mission, summarising the survey characteristics, the various data-processing steps, and data products. We also highlight the main science objectives and expected performance.

papers.title: A Remote-Sensing Application in Extended Fisheries Reserach
papers.abstract: As known that satellite captures most spectral signatures of any certain dimension oriented water-bodies and may useful in fisheries resource management. Satellite imagery can tell the value of Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) which is among important water quality parameters and can be detected digitally. This digital value is a prime aquatic parameter and may be termed as a principal component parameter to determine species existences in most geographic and breeding habitat of aquatic organisms. A scientific study found that Marine aquatic species may breed naturally within the TDS value, below 250 ppm. Never to forget that most aquatic species may breed during the rainy season and rain water has got a TDS value in a range of 5-50 ppm. On the other side a study found that most sweat water inland aquatic species may breed naturally within below the TDS of 150 ppm. This value of TDS measure act to insert osmotic pressure to the individual aquatic species and also to the reproductive cells. Study found that every species has got a very specific tolerance of osmotic pressure and may be uniquely sensitized by individual species. Today computer and electronics like a mere TDS meter digitally can identify such aquatic requirements of species. However satellite imagery in a large extent may identify the habitat distributions and identification of breeding zones of every individual species either in inland or marine environments to keep aquatic species safer.

question: How can machine learning algorithms be applied to the real-time control and optimization of single-ion transport in memory devices to enhance picosecond switching performance and energy efficiency?
hypothesis: Implementing a deep reinforcement learning algorithm for real-time control of single-ion transport in a memory device will achieve sub-picosecond switching times and reduce energy consumption by at least 25% compared to traditional voltage-pulse control methods.
methodology: The student will first generate a dataset of single-ion transport dynamics through a monolayer h-BN vacancy using molecular dynamics simulations (e.g., LAMMPS) or by curating published first-principles data. This dataset will capture ion positions, applied voltage pulses, and resulting switching times and energy consumption. Next, a deep reinforcement learning agent (e.g., DQN or PPO) will be trained in a simulated environment to optimize voltage pulse sequences in real-time, aiming to minimize switching time and energy. The model's performance will be evaluated against a baseline of fixed-pulse control strategies, measuring switching speed (sub-ps), energy (aJ/bit), and success rate over 1000 test episodes. The project will be implemented in Python using standard ML libraries, and results will be validated by comparing with experimental benchmarks from the literature, ensuring feasibility with undergraduate resources.
proposal: Recent advances in single-ion memory devices have demonstrated picosecond switching, but control remains based on fixed voltage pulses, limiting optimization. Despite the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to revolutionize atomic-scale control, no studies have applied machine learning to atom physics. This research aims to address this gap by investigating: How can machine learning algorithms be applied to the real-time control and optimization of single-ion transport in memory devices to enhance picosecond switching performance and energy efficiency? We hypothesize that implementing a deep reinforcement learning algorithm for real-time control of single-ion transport in a memory device will achieve sub-picosecond switching times and reduce energy consumption by at least 25% compared to traditional voltage-pulse control methods. The methodology involves generating a dataset of ion transport dynamics through a monolayer h-BN vacancy via molecular dynamics simulations, training a deep reinforcement learning agent (e.g., DQN or PPO) to optimize voltage pulse sequences in real-time, and evaluating performance against baseline fixed-pulse strategies using metrics such as switching speed, energy per bit, and success rate. Expected contributions include the first demonstration of AI-driven control in atom-scale systems, paving the way for ultra-fast and energy-efficient memory technologies and advancing the integration of AI with atom physics research.
